data.hypothesis: The failed prior attempt passes n=32 but fails at n=128, consistent with reloading C on later reduction panels even though the partial register sums were never stored. This candidate retains each 4x4 microkernel's accumulators across all K panels and stores each output once. It also tests increasing the row tile from 64 to 128 while holding the 64-column and 64-K tiles, scalar microkernel, and flattened static tile ownership constant. Fewer tile tasks may reduce scheduling work at n=1024; reduced parallelism may instead hurt smaller sizes. Earlier valid flattened parallel and row-band means were 0.033899 s and 0.035286 s, respectively; no speedup is claimed before measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Register-accumulating GEMM microkernels that defer output stores must not reload C between reduction panels unless partial sums were actually written.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior candidate's n=32 cases passed while n=128 failed with 16,375 errors; its source reloaded C for later K panels without storing the earlier register sums.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate the corrected accumulator across all official sizes, then compare repeated n=1024 timings against the measured flattened-tile variant.

data.notes: The proposed change fixes the prior multi-panel accumulation correctness issue and tests a 128-row output tile. Packing, scratch allocation, explicit SIMD, and a separate C-zeroing pass are intentionally omitted. The controller must validate correctness and measure the candidate; previous times are measured observations, not predictions.
transformations: Keep the 4x4 scalar output microkernel and 64-element reduction panels, but retain register accumulators across every panel instead of rereading C before any partial output has been stored.
Increase the output row tile to 128 while retaining 64-column tiles and flattened static ownership of independent tiles.
Continue to cap OpenMP workers by the caller's thread count and available tile count, with serial fallback when OpenMP is unavailable or one worker is requested.
Retain bounds-safe scalar handling for incomplete tiles and write every C element on each call without a separate initialization pass.
